question: From how many coffee trees does most of the arabica grown in Latin America descend?
answer: A handful, chiefly one. Dutch traders took coffee from Yemen to Java; in 1706 a Javan plant reached Amsterdam's botanical garden. A descendant given to Louis XIV in 1714 stocked the Paris hothouse; seedlings from these two founded plantations in Suriname and Martinique. That Typica line, with Bourbon from Réunion, underlies most Latin American coffee.
move: When a whole region grows one plant, ask how few it started from.
ask: Where am I relying on one source, supplier or idea that all my results grew from?
source: Anthony et al., Theor. Appl. Genet., 2002
reference: Anthony, Combes, Astorga, Bertrand, Graziosi & Lashermes, The origin of cultivated Coffea arabica L. varieties revealed by AFLP and SSR markers, Theoretical and Applied Genetics, 2002
